actions.blurb: A studio is your program: a roster, the work you assign, and a join code you give out once. Everything else in IPT hangs off it.
actions.name: createStudio
actions.title: Starting a studio

actions.blurb: A performer enters the code their instructor gave them and lands in the studio, with whatever is assigned this week on screen. There is nothing else to set up.
actions.name: joinStudio
actions.title: Joining a studio

actions.blurb: Assign a piece with a weekly target and notes on what to work on: hands separate, take it at 72, sticking as written. Your notes are in the app, so a performer reads them while they practice.
actions.name: assignWork
actions.title: Assigning the work

actions.blurb: A performer starts a session before they play and stops it when they are done, so the time is counted rather than remembered. Sessions are saved on the device before they are sent, so a practice room with no signal does not lose them.
actions.name: logPractice
actions.title: Logging a session

actions.blurb: A performer can attach a short recording to a session, and can flag the moments they want heard. IPT never stops another app's metronome, so anything playing in the room is captured with them.
actions.name: recordTake
actions.title: Recording a take

actions.blurb: Each instruction on the plan gets ticked off as it is worked. Ticks are not scored. They are there so a performer can see what is left.
actions.name: markFocusPoint
actions.title: Ticking off the plan

actions.blurb: You listen to a take and send one line back, and the performer is told when you do. It goes one direction: no thread and no reply.
actions.name: acknowledgeSession
actions.title: Saying you heard it

actions.blurb: One line to one performer, to reach somebody who has gone quiet. They can read it and mark it seen. There is no thread and no reply.
actions.name: sendNudge
actions.title: Sending one line

actions.blurb: Promote an assistant to instructor, correct what this studio shows for somebody, or remove a performer who has left.
actions.name: manageRoster
actions.title: Running the roster

actions.blurb: Tune what earns points, or switch the leaderboard off entirely and the standings disappear. The one thing IPT will not store is a set of weights where raw minutes outscore finishing the work.
actions.name: setScoring
actions.title: How the studio scores

actions.blurb: Tell IPT when your program is in session. Weeks outside a term do not count against anybody, so a summer off does not end every streak in the studio.
actions.name: setTerms
actions.title: When the studio is running

actions.blurb: A performer's name, instrument and color are what the studio sees beside their practice. There are no photographs anywhere in IPT.
actions.name: editProfile
actions.title: Your profile

actions.blurb: An account carries your studios, your practice and your recordings, on every device you sign in on. The demo needs none of it, which is why it is open to anybody.
actions.name: createAccount
actions.title: Your own account

actions.blurb: A real account can be deleted from inside the app, and IPT names what that destroys before it happens: the studios, the people and the hours. The demo has no account to delete.
actions.name: deleteAccount
actions.title: Deleting an account

instructor.body: Set a target for one performer or the whole studio, and add notes on what to work on: hands separate, take it at 72, fix the release in bar 12. Your notes stay on the screen while they practice, and each line can be ticked off as it is worked.
instructor.title: Assignments, with a weekly target

instructor.body: A performer can attach a short recording to a session and flag the moments they want heard. IPT never stops another app's metronome, so whatever is playing in the room is captured with them. An instructor can turn recording off for a whole studio.
instructor.title: Optional recordings

instructor.body: It lists the performers who are behind before the ones who are fine, rather than in alphabetical order. Open somebody's week, hear anything they sent, and write a line back.
instructor.title: A dashboard that sorts itself

instructorQuestions.answer: Everything you assigned that week, finished. Time rounds down, so 44 minutes of a 45-minute target is not met. IPT never credits a minute somebody did not practice.
instructorQuestions.question: What counts as a week being met?

instructorQuestions.answer: A week you assigned nothing in is not a week anybody failed. If your program has real breaks, set them under Terms, and weeks outside a term stop counting against anybody. Without that, a summer off would end every streak in the studio.
instructorQuestions.question: Why did somebody's streak not break over the holidays?

instructorQuestions.answer: Yes, and the performer can flag the moments they want you to hear. Listen to all plays them one at a time, and takes one from each performer before it comes back for anybody's second.
instructorQuestions.question: Can I see how long a recording is before I play it?

instructorQuestions.answer: Practice is saved on their own device before it is sent, so a room with no signal does not lose it. It appears for you when their app next has a connection. If a session says it could not be added to the studio, the assignment it belonged to was probably deleted.
instructorQuestions.question: A performer's practice isn't showing up.

instructorQuestions.answer: You → Scoring → No points. The standings disappear rather than sitting there empty, and assignments, practice and recordings work exactly the same. Plenty of programs run without a leaderboard.

performer.body: Stop it when you are done and IPT keeps the time for you. What your instructor asked for stays on the screen while you practice. If you forget to start a session, you can write it down afterward.
performer.title: Start a session before you play

performer.body: Recording is optional. If you add one, your instructor can hear how it sounded and write back about it. Mark this spot flags a moment for them, while you record or when you play it back afterwards, so they go straight to the part you meant.
performer.title: Add a recording if you want to

performer.body: They can listen to what you send and write back. Nobody else in the studio can hear your recordings or read your notes. They only see that you practiced, and for how long.
performer.title: Only your instructor hears it

performerQuestions.answer: Your instructors, and nobody else. The rest of the studio can see that you practiced and for how long, but never your recordings, and never the notes you write.
performerQuestions.question: Who can hear my recordings?

performerQuestions.answer: Anything under two minutes is not counted, and IPT tells you when that happens, so a start you did not mean does not become a session you did not practice.
performerQuestions.question: Does a really short session count?

performerQuestions.answer: It is safe. Sessions are saved on this device before they go anywhere, so nothing is lost in a room with no signal. It goes out by itself the next time you have a connection.
performerQuestions.question: My practice says it is waiting to send.

performerQuestions.answer: Minutes always round down, so 44 minutes of a 45-minute target is not met. It works the same way for everybody in the studio.
performerQuestions.question: Why did my time round down?

performerQuestions.answer: No. A session counts without one. A recording is what lets your instructor hear how it sounded and write back about it.
